7 Easy Fall Day Trips from Loveland, Colorado — 2025 Edition

You don’t need a long vacation to experience fall’s best views. From Loveland, you’re a short drive from mountain vistas, quiet forest roads, and cozy small-town stops. These seven day trips deliver the color and charm that make Northern Colorado special.

1. Estes Park & Rocky Mountain National Park

Take Highway 34 through Big Thompson Canyon and watch the slopes turn gold. Elk sightings, crisp air, and endless photo opportunities. Local tip: stop at Coffee on the Rocks—peaceful pond, great coffee, and memorable duck cameos.

2. Devil’s Backbone Open Space (Loveland)

Minutes from home. Sunset views, red-rock backdrops, and trails that glow at dusk—perfect for a spontaneous hike or photo session.

3. Horsetooth Reservoir

Pack a picnic and enjoy cottonwood reflections across the water. Evening light makes it ideal for photos.

4. Poudre Canyon

Winding roads, waterfalls, and pull-offs for riverside breaks—an easy way to feel worlds away.

5. Old Town Fort Collins

Local coffee, boutiques, live music, and brick-lined charm. Tip: warm cider at Bean Cycle Roasters, then a stroll through the art alleys behind Walnut Street.

6. Canyon Lakes Ranger District

Quiet forest roads, fiery aspens, and wildlife sightings with fewer crowds.

7. Cheyenne, Wyoming

Antique shops, western history, and an easy day that feels like a step back in time.

Mid-post CTA: See these locations on video and get more local tips: watch the fall day-trip tour.

Frequently Asked Questions

When is peak fall color in Northern Colorado?

Typically late September through early October, depending on elevation and weather.

Which trip is most family-friendly?

Estes Park and RMNP—easy trails, wildlife, and amenities.

Can you drive through Devil’s Backbone?

No—hiking trails provide the best views. The trailheads are close to town and easy to access.
